It provides the exact Upload signature and reuses multipartbody.NewFile, while A invents a different option API and explicitly adds forbidden association machinery.","reasons":["B implements `Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption)`, exactly matching the required public API; A instead accepts `...UploadFileOption`.","B directly reuses the established `internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content)` helper. A expands that helper with duplicate field-encoding machinery.","A adds deal, person, organization, product, activity, lead, and project association options, directly violating the contract's prohibition on adding association fields and changing FilesOption behavior.","Both patches fail the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add, but B at least mirrors existing FilesOption query/request-option handling, whereas A creates a parallel option system and request path semantics unrelated to Add's options modelB's multipart and retry tests verify field name, filename, content, validation, and complete content on both attempts. A covers similar behavior but tests its out-of-contract association API as a major part of the feature."],"risks_a":["Public Upload signature is incompatible with the frozen contract.","Introduces forbidden association APIs and `NewFileWithFields`, increasing API surface and maintenance burden.","Bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates response/request handling directly through Raw.Do Changes unrelated retry machinery and documents broader behavior changes beyond scopeNo explicit source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating its request construction, response decoding, and missing-data handling instead of centralizing behavior.","The global RawClient seekable-body refactor is outside the requested scope and changes Content-Length and caller-owned reader closing semantics.","No explicit test verifies propagation of an error returned by the source readerThe Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a deliberately non-replayable streaming source, so it does not strongly prove that initial source replayability is irrelevant after buffering."]}
